title: 10.4 A 2- TRX IR-UWB Transceiver with Shared Antennas Supporting Channels 5 to 12 in Compliance with IEEE 802.15.4/4z Standards
problem: IR-UWB transceivers must support multiple channels (5-12) to reduce interference in crowded 6GHz spectrum while minimizing cost through antenna sharing, but previous integrated RF switches suffer high insertion loss degrading receiver sensitivity.
motivation: UWB IoT/mobile/automotive expansion creates multi-user interference in congested spectrum; supporting multiple channels requires efficient integration while sharing antennas to reduce BOM cost.
method: The chip includes two integrated transceivers (receiver-transmitter pairs) for impulse radio ultra-wideband (IR-UWB)—a communication technique using short radio pulses across a wide frequency range—supporting channels 5 through 12 to operate in the crowded 6GHz spectrum without interfering with each other. Both transceivers share transmit and receive antennas through integrated RF switches (electronic gates that route signals), designed to minimize insertion loss—the weakening of signal strength as it passes through. By keeping insertion loss low, the receivers maintain their sensitivity despite signal routing, and the entire system is built as a single integrated circuit using CMOS technology in compliance with IEEE 802.15.4/4z standards.
key_novelty: The core innovation is designing integrated RF switches that reduce both insertion loss and noise figure degradation compared to prior CMOS designs, enabling two transceivers to reliably share antennas without sacrificing receiver sensitivity.
contributions: Fully integrated RF switches eliminating external SOI switches and SiP cost
Reduced insertion loss and noise figure vs prior CMOS switch implementations
primary_theme: integrated multi-channel IR-UWB transceiver with shared antennas
